newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank securities unit in settlement.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank securities unit in settlement.

text.p: NationsBank Corp and Florida regulators said Tuesday they have agreed to a settlement which puts an end to an investigation of sales practices in the bank's securities unit.

According to a news release issued by Florida's Office of the Comptroller and by the state attorney general, NationSecurities agreed to an independent review of its activities. The securities unit also agreed to establish an arbitration program and to make payments to the state totaling $850,000.

"We have moved forward from 1994 and we are glad to put this behind us," said NationsBank executive vice president John Munce in a telephone interview. He noted that the probe covered activities that occurred in 1993 and 1994.
"We believe that the spirit of the agreement which creates the education fund is consistent with our objective at all times, which is to to meet the financial needs of our customers," Munce said.
NationsBank, based in Charlotte, N.C., is the fourth-largest U.S. bank holding company with about $239 billion in assets.

"This settlement will provide greater oversight and consumer protection, while at the same time eliminating potentially lengthy legal proceedings," Florida comptroller Robert Milligan said in a statement. Milligan was joined in the announcement by Florida attorney general Bob Butterworth.
The agreement establishes a dispute resolution process to resolve customer complaints on file with the department and handle the payment of any claims resulting from the dispute.
The settlement requires NationsSecurities to contract with an independent consultant to review broker-dealer compliance functions and to report to the comptroller within 120 days.

Barry Harris, general counsel of NationSecurities, who participated in the telephone interview along with Munce, said representatives of a law firm and a big six accounting firm would update a review that was undertaken voluntarily more than two years ago.
Harris said the only cost to the company would be the $850,000 paid to the state and the cost of the dispute resolution process.
Asked if any NationSecurities personnel were subject to any discipline, Harris said there were "a few cases" but he could not recall the details of any specific case.

The $850,000 payment to the state is broken down into three components. NationSecurities will pay $250,000 to establish an investor education program in Florida. The agreement provides that $300,000 will be paid to the Office of the Attorney General's Legal Affairs Revolving Trust Fund. Also, $300,000 will go to the Department of Banking and Finance to cover legal fees and investigative costs.

NationSecurities also agreed to undertake certain business practices, including adopting a disclosure form to accompany all investment sales. The firm will maintain a ratio of at least one supervisor for every 25 brokers selling investments.
Harris noted that the settlement stipulated that there was no finding that NationsSecurities violated any law.

Munce, in response to a question, said Boatmen's Investment Services, part of Boatmen's Bancshares which was acquired by NationsBank earlier this year, is being combined with NationSecurities. He said the result will be a single broker-dealer serving customers nationwide.
